content.intro: Learn custom model fields through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Custom Model Fields matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines custom model fields as part of advanced django architecture. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Field behavior; Serialization and database representation; Migration implications; Validation; Testing compatibility across database backends. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Field behavior
items.text: Field behavior affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Validation
items.text: For Validation, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Testing compatibility across database backends
items.text: A good test covers an observable contract and asserts status, output, database changes or access denial. Include invalid and boundary inputs so a regression does not only fail on a happy path.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Custom Model Fields
content_blocks.code:
from django.db import models

class Product(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    sku = models.CharField(max_length=40, unique=True)
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
content_blocks.expected_output: The model declares bounded text, a unique identifier and an explicit default.

content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Field behavior. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
